title: Interleaved Bitstream Execution for Multi-Pattern Regex Matching on GPUs
problem: Bitparallel regex engines compile regular expressions into bitstream programs that expose fine-grained instruction-level parallelism well-suited for GPU execution, but the naive sequential (per-instruction loop-over-data) execution model suffers from poor data reuse — each data block is loaded multiple times across instructions — and high memory consumption from intermediate bitstream state, limiting GPU throughput.
motivation: Pattern matching is a critical and performance-sensitive operation in unstructured data analytics (log processing, network intrusion detection, text search), and GPU-accelerated regex engines are increasingly important, but fundamental memory access inefficiencies prevent them from reaching peak GPU throughput.
method: The paper fuses all the pattern-matching instructions into a single loop that processes one data block at a time, so each block gets loaded once from memory and processed by all instructions before moving to the next block. To handle the fact that later instructions depend on results from earlier blocks, they use selective recomputation—recalculating parts of the dependency chain when needed rather than having threads communicate with each other. They also restructure these dependency chains to reduce the depth of synchronization barriers between groups of GPU threads (warps), and skip computation entirely on data blocks that are all zeros, since sparse patterns often produce zero results.
key_novelty: Instead of running one pattern-matching instruction across all data blocks before running the next instruction, this approach fuses all instructions into a single loop that processes one block at a time, improving data reuse and avoiding intermediate storage, while resolving dependencies through selective recalculation rather than inter-thread communication.
contributions: Interleaved bitstream execution model fusing all regex instructions into a single block-wise loop to maximize data reuse on GPU.
Dependency-Aware Thread-Data Mapping that resolves cross-block bitstream dependencies via selective recomputation, making interleaved execution correct on GPU.
Shift Rebalancing optimization that balances dependency chain depth to reduce GPU synchronization barrier count.
Zero Block Skipping optimization exploiting bitstream sparsity to skip zero-valued intermediate blocks; combined system achieves 19.5x geometric mean speedup over state-of-the-art GPU regex engine.

metrics.speedup: 19.5x geometric mean speedup over state-of-the-art GPU regex engine
